samples.summary: No test covers undo/redo of a paste that created or dropped merged blocks
samples.evidence: `paste` now mutates the merge map (`applyPasteMerges` → `store.setMerge`/`store.deleteMerge`) and deletes content under newly created blocks (`clearCellsUnderMerge`). The only undo/redo test added (merge.test.ts ~1109, 'should drop the copy buffer on undo and redo') stubs `MemStore.undo`/`redo` to return `{success:true}` and replay nothing, so it only asserts the buffer is cleared. Nothing asserts that undoing a merge-carrying paste restores the previous merge layout and the cells cleared under the pasted block. If store history does not record merge ops, an undo leaves a stale merged block and permanently-deleted covered content — visible layout/data corruption.
searchedFor: grep undo|redo in packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts and clipboard.test.ts

samples.summary: The view-level removal of `clearCopyBuffer()` after paste is untested
samples.evidence: Both `Worksheet.pasteFromClipboard` (worksheet.ts ~4947) and `Spreadsheet.paste` (spreadsheet.ts ~724) dropped their `clearCopyBuffer()` call — the behavioral point of the change (repeat pastes stay internal, a refused paste keeps the clipboard). The only coverage is model-level (merge.test.ts 'should propagate merges on a second paste from the same copy' / 'should keep the copy buffer when a paste is refused'), which calls `sheet.paste` directly. Re-introducing the view-level clear would leave every test green while silently demoting repeat pastes to external ones.

samples.summary: The `revalidateCopyBuffer()` call on the remote-change path is untested
samples.evidence: merge.test.ts:1150-1184 tests `Sheet.revalidateCopyBuffer` by calling it directly with a hand-rolled `AxisIdStore`. No test exercises the wiring added in `worksheet.ts:5248` (the remote reload path), so removing that call — which is the only thing that drops a stale index-keyed buffer after a peer's structural edit — would not fail any test.
searchedFor: grep in packages/sheets/test/view for remote/reload handlers

samples.summary: No test that `sortFilterByColumn` clears the copy buffer
samples.evidence: `sortFilterByColumn` gained `this.clearCopyBuffer()` (sheet.ts:4009) with the rationale that a sort renumbers the cells the buffer snapshotted. Tests exist for the insert path and the reorder path (merge.test.ts:89-128) but none for sort: `packages/sheets/test/sheet/filter.test.ts` calls `sortFilterByColumn` at lines 203/226/260/325 and never touches `copy()`/`getCopyRange()`.

samples.summary: Drag-reorder's new `if (!moved) return` selection guard is untested at the view level
samples.evidence: `moveRows`/`moveColumns` now return a boolean and the drag-reorder completion handler skips re-selecting when the move was refused. The model-side boolean is covered (merge.test.ts 'should report whether a row reorder actually happened'), but nothing exercises the view handler, so a regression that re-selects a destination the rows never reached would ship silently.

samples.summary: Column-axis freeze/merge interaction is untested on both new backend guards and on `moveCells`
samples.evidence: backend worksheet.controller.spec.ts only tests rows (`{rows:2, cols:0}`) for both the snap and the 409; worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts only adds row-axis cases for `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`; and in sheet.ts `moveCells`' new `merge-move-frozen` check is only covered for `moveRows` (merge.test.ts 'should refuse a row reorder that lands a block across the boundary'). The `frozenCols` branch of `crossesFreezePane`/`snapFreezePastMerges` is only reached by the `insertColumns` snap test, so a column-axis regression in the API guards would pass CI.

`snapshotMergesIn` deliberately excludes a merged block the copied range only clips (`filter(isRangeInRange)`), documented as a guard for programmatic callers. No test copies a range that clips a block and asserts the paste carries no merge; merge.test.ts's copy-paste cases all copy whole blocks.
searchedFor: read new 'Sheet merge + copy-paste' describe block in merge.test.ts

samples.summary: The new spill re-attempt wiring on the paste path (`unblockedAnchors`) is untested
samples.evidence: `paste` now threads `unblockedAnchors` through `applyPasteMerges`/`clearCellsUnderMerge` and seeds them into the dependants map so a previously blocked spill anchor re-spills. No test in the new merge.test.ts blocks — grep for 'spill' in packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts returns no matches — so pasting a merged block over a spill blocker or over a spill anchor's ghosts is entirely uncovered; a failure would silently leave a formula un-spilled or orphan ghost cells.

samples.summary: Backend spec's plain-object doc mock cannot verify the documented rollback-on-throw
samples.evidence: The spec's `doc.update` is `(fn) => fn(root)` with no transaction, so `expect(ws().merges).toEqual({})` only proves the guard runs before the assignment, not the comment's claim that 'a throw inside `doc.update` rolls the whole update back'. (The structure-axis spec, by contrast, uses a real yorkie Document.) Low cost, but the assertion is weaker than it reads.

samples.summary: New refusal message strings have no test
samples.evidence: `refusalMessage` gained `merge-paste-partial`, `merge-paste-frozen` and `merge-move-frozen` cases; grep shows no test anywhere asserts `refusalMessage` output (only the model-level refusal codes are asserted). Consistent with the pre-existing cases, hence nit.

finding.summary: No test covers undo/redo of a paste that created or dropped merged blocks
finding.evidence: `paste` now mutates the merge map (`applyPasteMerges` → `store.setMerge`/`store.deleteMerge`) and deletes content under newly created blocks (`clearCellsUnderMerge`). The only undo/redo test added (merge.test.ts ~1109, 'should drop the copy buffer on undo and redo') stubs `MemStore.undo`/`redo` to return `{success:true}` and replay nothing, so it only asserts the buffer is cleared. Nothing asserts that undoing a merge-carrying paste restores the previous merge layout and the cells cleared under the pasted block. If store history does not record merge ops, an undo leaves a stale merged block and permanently-deleted covered content — visible layout/data corruption.
searchedFor: grep undo|redo in packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts and clipboard.test.ts

verdict.reason: The factual observation is accurate (no test asserts undo restores a merge layout after a paste), but it is not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric. (a) The paste behavior this change adds IS meaningfully covered: merge.test.ts:385-728 holds 20 tests including store-level persistence of the created block (merge.test.ts:408-425 asserts store.getMerges()), destination-block drop (448-468), dependant recalculation (470), stale-data-under-merge (496) and the refusal paths. (b) Undo replay is store-history behavior that cannot be tested meaningfully in this package: MemStore.undo/redo return {success:false} and beginBatch/endBatch are explicit no-ops (memory.ts:674-696), so any 'undo restores merges' test here would have to stub undo exactly as the existing test does — the over-mocked/vacuous shape this lens rejects. (c) The undo seam is generic and unchanged by this diff: Sheet.undo/redo already reload merges from the store (sheet.ts:5368, 5402), and the only real history store writes merges as ordinary doc.update ops on the same batched path as every cell write (yorkie-store.ts:961-1008, 77-79), the same path mergeSelection (sheet.ts:4896) and moveRangeTo (sheet.ts:2936-2944) already used. The finding's stated failure mode ('if store history does not record merge ops') is a store-layer correctness question, outside this lens. I found no counterexample test, so I refute on scope rather than on an existing test.

finding.summary: The test claiming to cover the new freeze-snap inside `shiftCells` never triggers the snap
finding.evidence: `it('should keep the freeze clear of a block when rows are inserted')` merges A2:A4, calls setFreezePane(2,0) (already snapped to 4 by `setFreezePane`), then `insertRows(1, 1)`. In `shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1392-1417) the pre-existing branch `count > 0 && index <= frozen` already yields frozenRows = 5, and the shifted block A3:A5 satisfies range[1].r (5) > rows (5) === false, so `snapFreezePastMerges` at sheet.ts:1422 makes no change. The asserted `{ frozenRows: 5, frozenCols: 0 }` holds identically with the whole new snap block deleted — it is fake coverage for that block. No test in the diff or in packages/sheets/test/sheet/freeze-pane.test.ts drives a structural edit that actually leaves a block straddling the boundary (e.g. deleting rows inside the frozen area so a block ends up half-frozen, or inserting rows inside a block that sits on the boundary), which is exactly the state the new code exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: Two independent checks refute the finding. (a) The test it names, `it('should keep the freeze clear of a block when rows are inserted')`, does not exist anywhere in packages/sheets (grep for "keep the freeze clear" → no matches). The nearest real test, merge.test.ts:815 'should carry a frozen block down with an insert above it', is explicitly documented at lines 825-827 as covering the pre-existing boundary adjustment with "no snapping needed", so it is not presented as coverage for the new snap block. (b) The substantive claim that no test drives a structural edit leaving a block straddling the boundary is false: merge.test.ts:833-858 seeds a straddling block through the store/load path (store.setMerge A3:A5, store.setFreezePane(3,0)) then insertRows(1,1) — the pre-existing branch at sheet.ts:1392-1394 yields frozenRows 4 while the merge shifts to A4:A6, which still straddles (merging.ts:221: 4<=4 && 6>4 → rows=6). The test asserts frozenRows 6 and that it was persisted via store.getFreezePane(), values only reachable through the new snap at sheet.ts:1418-1423; with that block removed the value is 4 and the test fails. merge.test.ts:860-874 does the equivalent on the column axis (frozenCols 5 vs 3 without the snap). The claimed fake/missing coverage is therefore not as described.
